==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|morwenynge}}, from {{af|enm|morwen|-ynge|nocat=1}}. {{surf|en|morn|-ing}}. See also {{m|en|morrow}} ({{cog|enm|morwe}}).

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈmɔːnɪŋ/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈmoːnɪŋ/|a=SSB,AU,NZ}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-morning.ogg|a=SSB|IPA=[ˈmoːnɪi̯ŋ]}} 
* {{IPA|en|/ˈmoɹnɪŋ/|a=GA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-morning.ogg|a=US|IPA=[ˈmõ̞ɹ̃nɪ̃i̯ŋ]}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈmɔːnɪŋɡ/|a=Northern England,Midlands,non-ng-coalescence!without NG-coalescence}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈmoɹnɪŋ/|a=IE}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈmɑːɹnən/|/-nəŋ/|a=Dublin}}
* {{a|en|non-horse-hoarse}}
:* {{IPA|en|/mɔɾnɪŋ/|a=Scotland}}
:* {{IPA|en|/mɔːnɪŋɡ/|a=Manchester}}
:* {{IPA|en|/mɒnɪŋ/|a=Eastern New England}}
:* {{IPA|en|/mɔɹnɪŋ/|a=early 20th century <<GA>>,near-obsolete}}
:* {{IPA|en|/mɔːnɪŋ/|a=19th century <<RP>>}}
* {{hyphenation|en|morn|ing}}
* {{homophones|en|mourning|aa=horse-hoarse}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)nɪŋ|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{wp}}
{{en-noun}}

# The early [[part]] of the [[day]], especially from [[midnight]] to [[noon]]. {{defdate|from 13th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'll see you tomorrow '''morning'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'm working in the '''morning''', so let's meet in the afternoon.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1835|author=Sir {{w|John Ross (Arctic explorer)|John Ross}}; Sir {{w|James Clark Ross}}|title=[http://books.google.com.au/books?id=SdQBAAAAYAAJ Narrative of a Second Voyage in Search of a North-west Passage …]|volume=1|pages=284–5
|passage=Towards the following '''morning''', the thermometer fell to 5°; and at daylight, there was not an atom of water to be seen in any direction.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=4|passage=One '''morning''' I had been driven to the precarious refuge afforded by the steps of the inn, after rejecting offers from the Celebrity to join him in a variety of amusements. But even here I was not free from interruption, for he was seated on a horse-block below me, playing with a fox terrier.}}
# {{lb|en|figurative}} The early part of anything. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} That part of the day from dawn until the main meal (typically in late afternoon). {{defdate|18th–19th c.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1791|author=w:Charlotte Smith|title=Celestina|publisher=Broadview|year_published=2004|page=101
|passage=Celestina {{...}} retired to her own room, leaving her friend to the pleasing and important occupation of the toilet, in which half of what is now called '''morning''', was usually passed by Matilda.}}
#* '''1813''', {{w|Jane Austen}}, letter, 26 October:
# {{lb|en|chiefly|Scotland}} The first alcoholic drink of the day; a [[morning draught]]. {{defdate|from 18th c.}}

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|time from dawn to noon}} {{l|en|forenoon}}; {{l|en|yeender}} {{qualifier|dialect}}; see also [[Thesaurus:morning]]
* {{sense|time from midnight to noon}} {{l|en|a.m.}}; {{l|en|forenoon}}; {{l|en|yeender}} {{qualifier|dialect}}

====Coordinate terms====
* {{l|en|afternoon}}; {{l|en|evening}}; {{l|en|night}}
